Coordinator note, operator direction on 2026-09-27, with the first incident recorded under it.

The operator said: "If there are recurrent tracking activity failures like project field edits, that is something we need a process circuit breaker on that which manifests as a process incident that pauses work and needs to be resolved."

Requirement to fold into the body: a circuit breaker on tracking failures. Tracking activity means writes that keep GitHub in step with the work: Project field edits, issue and pull request state changes, labels, and role comments. When such a write fails repeatedly, the breaker opens, a process incident is declared, new work is paused, and work resumes only when the incident is resolved and the missed writes are applied. The procedure defines the threshold, for example three failures of the same kind within ten minutes, what pausing covers, who closes the breaker, and the record. The check must read the rate limit from response headers, because the summary endpoint reported a full budget while requests were being refused.

Incident record, first use.

- Declared: 2026-09-27 00:22 America/New_York, by the coordinator.
- What failed: Project field edits as `tbhb`, from about 00:10. About forty edits failed with `unknown owner type`.
- Cause, verified: the GraphQL budget of `tbhb` was exhausted. Response headers showed limit 5000, used 5000, remaining 0. The reviewer account was not affected.
- Cause of the exhaustion, inference: nine workers at once, whose `gh pr` and `gh issue` subcommands use GraphQL although the briefs say REST, plus a batch of Project edits by the coordinator.
- Contributing error: the coordinator read the summary endpoint, which reported a full budget, and misjudged the failure as a secondary limit.
- Effect: the board understates progress. Priority, phase, and status edits are pending for about forty items.
- Action: new launches that act as `tbhb` are paused until the budget resets and the pending edits are applied. Reviews by the reviewer account continue, because its budget is separate. Running workers were left to finish.
- To resolve: apply the pending edits after the reset, confirm the board matches the work, then lift the pause.
- Follow-up proposed: a wrapper that uses REST only for the common pull request and issue operations, a budget check from headers before a batch of edits, and a lower limit on concurrent workers until then.

Coordinator note, incident resolution. The incident declared at 00:22 on 2026-09-27 and updated at 00:57 is resolved as of 01:14 America/New_York. The pause is lifted. The operator directed at about 01:00 that work would not wait for the GraphQL reset.

What was wrong

- Observed: `tbhbagent` had used 4981 of 5000 GraphQL points within about 21 minutes of its login. The window resets at 01:33:46.
- Observed: the fix round brief template told workers to run `gh pr checks <n> --watch`, two lines above a rule that forbade it. Worker logs show seven `--watch` invocations across the fix rounds for #137, #148, #174, and #175. The two runs with the most watches also logged the most rate limit errors, six and five.
- Inference: the per-item `gh project item-edit --url` retry loops were the largest consumer. Three loops from the previous session queued about 125 edits with retries. They left no log, so their cost is not measured.
- Observed: the REST `rate_limit` endpoint reported 4897 GraphQL points remaining while the response header of a GraphQL request said 19.

What changed

- Verified: the Project can be read and edited over REST, which spends the core budget and no GraphQL points. `GET users/tbhb/projectsV2/9/items` with a `fields` parameter returned all 143 items in two requests. `PATCH users/tbhb/projectsV2/9/items/<item id>` returned 200.
- Done: 88 field edits on 54 items were applied over REST with no failure, after the operator approved that path. Every open item now carries a Priority and a Phase. Items whose refinement verdict is ready moved to Ready. Phase 2 was used as the default for items that had no Phase, subject to the reorganization proposal.
- Done: the fix round template is REST only and names the check-runs path for CI.
- Done, operator approved: a polling ban in three layers. A `gh` shim, first on the worker `PATH` and kept first in login shells, refuses `gh pr checks`, `gh pr status`, `gh run watch`, `gh project`, and any `--watch` flag on `gh pr` or `gh run`, and logs each refusal. The Codex exec policy forbids the same commands in `~/.codex/rules/github-polling-ban.rules`. Claude Code deny rules cover them in the local settings of the main checkout.

Limits and open items

- Untested: a refusal inside a live Codex turn. The running workers carry the shim settings in their environment (verified), and the shim refused the command through a login shell in a local test (verified).
- Known gap: the Codex rules match by position, so a repository flag before the subcommand is covered only for this repository's name. The shim covers the general case.
- Open: the three old retry loops are still alive, because the coordinator session is not permitted to stop them. The operator has been asked to stop them before 01:33.
- Open: the Claude Code deny rules belong in the tracked project settings through a pull request. `handoff-state.sh` still reads the board with `gh project item-list` and needs the REST read. `gh pr view`, `gh pr list`, `gh issue view`, and `gh issue list` are a second phase of the ban, after the reviewer and author briefs move to REST.
